## CVE-2026-115731: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

Source-reported by [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2026-115731).

CVE-2026-115731 (official CVSS 9.4 and 9.9): Deserialization of untrusted data in the report-processing code of Puppet, as used by Puppet Server, in the affected releases, allows a client that holds any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as its service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type via PUT request. Where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain such a certificate. CISA lists it as exploited in the wild.

**What to do:** Apply the fix in the vendor's advisory (https://portal.perforce.com/s/cve/a91Qi000003IaHpIAK/report-deserialization-code-execution); the CVE record lists as affected: Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.0 before 2023.8.13; 2025.0.0 before 2025.12.1; 2026.0.0 before 2026.0.1. If no update or mitigation is available, take the product out of service.

| --- | --- | --- |
| CVE-2026-115731 exists | confirmed | [cve.org](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115731) |
| CVSS 9.4 | confirmed | [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115731) |
| exploited in the wild | confirmed | [CISA KEV](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2026-115731) |

Identifiers and scores checked automatically against cve.org and NVD.

**Limitations:** Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

Added to the CISA KEV catalog 17 Nov 2026; first seen by SecOpsAI 18 Nov 2026, 02:28 UTC.

## Collection scope

SecOpsAI watched 28 sources for this edition; all were current. 5 package registries are watched through release metadata only, without scanning package contents. This is not complete coverage of every source or registry.

## Credits and corrections

Prepared by Onyedika Christopher Agada. The editor approves each edition before it is published. Corrections keep the previous edition and explain material changes.
